extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their advisers (legal counsels, accountants, auditors) and investors
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and disclosure standards that public companies must follow when preparing climate-related disclosures in SEC filings, including emissions metrics, targets, assurance, tagging, and financial-statement impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of processes for identifying, assessing, and managing climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are required to disclose whether and how climate-related risks are integrated into the company's overall risk management system or processes, including both physical and transition risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investment Company Institute and other commenters support requiring this disclosure because it helps investors assess how companies determine materiality of climate-related risks and link those risks to strategy, business model, and outlook (citing letters in support). See also cross-reference to rule text (17 CFR references) cited in the surrounding discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from required disclosure about risk-assessment methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants will not be required to disclose, as applicable, how they: (1) determine the relative significance of climate-related risks compared to other risks; (2) consider existing or likely regulatory requirements or policies when identifying climate-related risks; (3) consider shifts in customer or counterparty preferences, technological changes, or changes in market prices in assessing potential transition risks; or (4) determine the materiality of climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicitly lists aspects of internal judgment and methodology that the Commission does not mandate registrants to explain in required climate-risk process disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material expenditures and material impacts on financial estimates/assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose material expenditures incurred and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions that (i) in management's assessment, directly result from activities to mitigate or adapt to climate-related risks, including adoption of new technologies or processes; or (ii) occur as a direct result of the target or goal or the actions taken to make progress toward meeting the target or goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 17 CFR 229.1502(d)(2) and 17 CFR 229.1504(c)(2). This requires linking mitigation/adaptation spending and target-related actions to material financial statement effects and describing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1% threshold for certain financial-statement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of a 1% threshold is used for disclosure of certain items within the financial statements, consistent with how the Commission currently treats similar disclosures in other contexts (e.g., §§210.5-03.1(a) and 210.12-13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule adopts a familiar quantitative cutoff (1%) for when certain disaggregated or quantified financial-statement effects should be reported, aligning climate-related disclosure thresholds with existing SEC practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of registrant's existing operational and organizational boundaries for emissions tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules enable registrants to continue to use the operational and organizational boundaries they already use to track emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits incremental burden by allowing continuity with current internal tracking methods; the discussion notes that costs for registrants who already track emissions will be limited for this reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline XBRL tagging of climate disclosures and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate disclosures and metrics must be tagged (inline XBRL) to facilitate machine readability and improve investor access, comparability, and understandability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites evidence that XBRL improves market efficiency, levels informational playing field, and enhances readability and informational value (multiple academic studies summarized). The final rules impose tagging requirements and explain expected investor benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable for tagging and compliance (filers categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large accelerated filers (LAFs) must begin complying with disclosure requirements in filings covering fiscal year 2025 and must comply with tagging requirements in filings covering fiscal year 2026. Other categories of filers must comply with tagging requirements upon their initial compliance with the climate disclosure rules. Accelerated filers (AFs) must comply with tagging requirements when they first provide climate disclosures in filings covering fiscal year 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the phased compliance schedule by filer type and links to section II.N of the rule text for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of whether/what type of assurance is obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should disclose whether they obtain assurance on climate-related disclosures and, if so, the types of assurance (and potentially the assuror's affiliation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC references commenters suggesting that, to encourage disclosure while the assurance industry matures, registrants disclose what types of assurance, if any, they are obtaining (an alternative to immediate mandatory attestation requirements). This disclosure can help investors assess credibility given heterogeneity among assurance providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of attestation/assurance industry maturity before mandatory attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission acknowledges concerns about availability and capacity of assurance providers and notes that as reporting and attestation standards develop and a standards-setting body emerges, the Commission may assess whether an attestation standard is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several commenters warned that attestation/certification of emissions is costlier and assurance-provider capacity may be insufficient; the rule discussion contemplates phased/matured approaches and refers to international practice where accountants frequently provide assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and heterogeneity of voluntary assurance reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC recognizes significant heterogeneity in content and scope of voluntary assurance reports and differences in metrics covered depending on the type of assuror (financial auditors vs non-financial assurers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation supports the Commission's attention to standardization and potential future policies regarding assurance; cited studies show voluntary assurance coverage rates and content variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of registrant shopping for favorable assurance conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may have incentives to search for a favorable assurance conclusion or opinion, paralleling documented rating-shopping behavior in other markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission cites literature on rating-shopping risk as a factor in considering how assurance/attestation requirements should be designed or disclosed to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to disclose financial-statement estimates/assumptions materially impacted by severe weather and other conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose financial-statement estimates and assumptions that are materially impacted by severe weather events and other conditions, as well as by disclosed targets or transition plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule notes that incremental costs include preparing these disclosures but expects the incremental costs to be minimal; cross-references include applicable Exchange Act rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaggregation of information consistent with U.S. GAAP/IFRS when required
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules align with existing U.S. GAAP and IFRS requirements to disaggregate certain information on the face of the financial statements or in notes when appropriate (e.g., ASC Topic 220 requires separate presentation of unusual/infrequent items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission notes that disaggregation is already required in other accounting contexts, reinforcing the practice for climate-related financial effects when material or unusual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of emissions targets, goals, and baseline years to enable investor assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require disclosure of registrants' emissions targets/goals and related information in ways that help investors identify potential 'cherry-picking' of baseline years and assess progress toward targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule cites research showing issuers may cherry-pick baseline years; the disclosure regime is intended to help investors detect such practices and form informed assessments of target progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of data-quality and measurement challenges (and link to assurance needs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission acknowledges studies showing quality issues in existing emissions databases (disparities, inaccurate third-party estimates) and that many registrants do not fully measure certain emissions categories (e.g., Scope 1), which affects the design and timing of assurance and disclosure expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contextual guidance informs why the Commission permits certain boundaries, phases tagging/assurance expectations, and emphasizes the role of assurance providers and standard setters in improving disclosure quality.
